faq.description: Everything you need to know about QRdx. For anything else, reach us at support@qrdx.dev

free.question: Is QRdx really free? Are there hidden limits?
free.answer: Yes. Creating, customizing and downloading static QR codes is free and needs no account: unlimited codes, every design option ({bodyPatterns, number} body patterns, {eyeShapes, number} corner-eye shapes and {eyeCentres, number} eye centers, gradients, logos, frames and Logo QR or Image QR art), and PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF and EPS downloads. There are no watermarks and no ads. Static codes store your content in the code itself, so they never expire and have no scan limits. A free account adds 10 dynamic QR codes, 3 hosted pages, {historyYears, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} of scan analytics, 10 saved themes and 5 AI theme generations; Pro ({proMonthly}/mo or {proYearly}/yr) and Business ({businessMonthly}/mo or {businessYearly}/yr) raise those limits.

signup.question: Do I need to sign up or create an account?
signup.answer: Not for static codes. Open the playground, enter your URL or content, customize the design and download it without signing up. Sign in (with GitHub or Google) when you want dynamic codes you can edit after printing, hosted pages, scan analytics, saved themes, community publishing or AI theme generation.

dynamic.question: Does QRdx support dynamic QR codes and scan analytics?
dynamic.answer: Yes. A dynamic code encodes a short link, so you can change where it points after printing, and every scan is counted with country, device and browser analytics. A code can open a website or a hosted mobile page (link list, menu, vCard, coupon, event, form, PDF, gallery, audio or video). Pro and Business add smart routing by device, country, language or time, A/B tests, UTM tags, passwords, expiry dates and scan limits. Free accounts get 10 active dynamic codes with {historyYears, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} of history; Pro and Business are unlimited and keep your full scan history.

guarantee.question: Will my QR codes stop working if I stop paying?
guarantee.answer: No. Under our Never-Hostage Guarantee every dynamic code keeps redirecting on every plan, including after a downgrade, a failed payment or a cancellation. Scans are unlimited and never paused, and we never show ads or send your scanners to a QRdx page. Plan limits only stop you creating new things. Static codes don't depend on QRdx at all.

compare.question: How does QRdx compare to QR Tiger, QR Code Monkey, or Flowcode?
compare.answer: QR TIGER and Flowcode are dynamic QR platforms: codes redirect through their service so you can edit them and track scans, and pricing grows with the number of codes. QR TIGER's free plan includes 3 dynamic codes with 500 scans each, and Flowcode's free plan allows 2 codes. QR Code Monkey, like QRdx, makes free static codes. QRdx does both: unlimited free static codes with deep styling, plus dynamic codes with unlimited scans on every plan, paid plans from {proMonthly} a month, and open-source code you can self-host. Our compare pages cover each tool in detail, including where it is the better choice.

logo.question: Can I add a logo to my QR code for free?
logo.answer: Yes. Logo overlay is included on the free tier. Upload an image (a PNG with a transparent background works best) and QRdx centers it and clears the modules underneath. QR codes use Reed-Solomon error correction (ISO/IEC 18004); QRdx defaults to level Q, which can recover roughly 25% of the code, so a centered logo stays scannable. Test with a few phones before printing.

openSource.question: Is QRdx open source?
openSource.answer: Yes. QRdx is open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0 (or later) and developed in public on GitHub. You can review the code, file issues, contribute, or self-host your own instance, dynamic codes and hosted pages included. The QR library is published on npm as qrdx for React apps. AGPL is a copyleft license, so check that it fits your project before embedding it in closed-source software.

api.question: Can developers generate QR codes with an API?
api.answer: Yes. The image API turns any URL into an SVG, PNG or EPS QR code with no API key, and the REST API, with a workspace API key or OAuth, creates and edits dynamic codes and reads their scans. There is also an MCP server for Claude, Cursor and VS Code, a command-line tool (@qrdx/cli), a shadcn/ui component and the qrdx React library.

paidPlans.question: What do I get with Pro or Business?
paidPlans.answer: Pro ({proMonthly}/mo or {proYearly}/yr) adds unlimited dynamic codes and hosted pages, your full scan history, {customDomains, select, yes {5 custom domains, } other {}}teams of up to 3, smart routing, A/B tests, UTM tags, pixels, email alerts and a weekly digest, and link controls such as passwords and expiry dates. Business ({businessMonthly}/mo or {businessYearly}/yr) adds white-label pages with custom CSS, {customDomains, select, yes {25 custom domains, } other {}}unlimited team members, conversion tracking, webhooks and Slack or Discord alerts. Creating, customizing and downloading static QR codes stays free.

faq.description: Billing, limits and what happens to your codes if you stop paying.

cancel.question: What happens if I cancel?
cancel.answer: Nothing breaks. Your plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for, then your account moves to Free. Every dynamic code keeps redirecting and every scan is still counted: that's our Never-Hostage Guarantee. On Free you can't create more than the Free limits allow, and analytics show the last {historyYears, plural, one {year} other {# years}}. Older scans are kept, so they come back if you upgrade again.

refund.question: Can I get my money back?
refund.answer: Yes. Your first payment for Pro or Business, monthly or yearly, comes with a {days, number}-day money-back guarantee: email support@qrdx.dev from your account's email address within {days, number} days of paying and we refund it in full, no questions asked. It's once per customer. Your codes keep working afterwards on the Free plan.

paymentFails.question: What happens if a payment fails?
paymentFails.answer: Your codes keep working. If the subscription lapses, your account follows the Free limits, exactly as if you had cancelled. We never pause codes, show ads, or send your scanners to a QRdx page because of billing.

scans.question: Do scans count against a limit?
scans.answer: No. Scans are unlimited on every plan and we never pause a code because of traffic. The only scan caps are the ones you set yourself on a code (Pro and Business).

rupees.question: Why do I see prices in ₹?
rupees.answer: Visitors from India see prices in Indian rupees: Pro is {proMonthly} a month or {proYearly} a year, Business {businessMonthly} a month or {businessYearly} a year. Checkout charges customers in India in ₹ and everyone else in US$, whichever currency you browsed in. Use the switch above the plans to change the display currency.

currencies.question: Why do I see prices in ₹ or €?
currencies.answer: Prices show in the currency of the country you're in. In India, Pro is {proMonthly} a month or {proYearly} a year and Business {businessMonthly} a month or {businessYearly} a year. In the EU and EEA, Pro is {proMonthlyEur} a month or {proYearlyEur} a year and Business {businessMonthlyEur} a month or {businessYearlyEur} a year. Everywhere else it's US$. Checkout charges the currency of your country, whichever currency you browsed in. Use the switch above the plans to change the display currency.

switchPlans.question: Can I switch plans or billing periods later?
switchPlans.answer: Yes. Open Manage subscription in your settings to change or cancel your plan in the Polar billing portal. Moving to a smaller plan never turns off existing codes, pages or domains.

teams.question: How do teams work on each plan?
teams.answer: Free accounts can't create teams. A Pro team has up to 3 members including the owner; a Business team has no member limit. A team's limits follow the best plan among its owners, and existing members stay if that plan changes.

selfHost.question: Can I self-host instead?
selfHost.answer: Yes. QRdx is open source under the AGPL-3.0. Run it with your own Postgres database by following the self-hosting guide; the plan limits are defined in one file that you can change for your instance.

faq.benefitQuestion: Which industries benefit most from QR codes?
faq.benefitAnswer: Any business that prints something a customer holds or walks past: menus, packaging, signs, tickets, labels and direct mail. The return is highest where information changes after printing (menus, prices, schedules, documents), because a dynamic code updates without a reprint.
faq.staticQuestion: Should a business use static or dynamic QR codes?
faq.staticAnswer: Use static codes for content that never changes, such as a Wi-Fi login, a payment ID or a contact card, because they are free and work without any service in between. Use dynamic codes for anything printed in volume or kept for months, so you can fix a wrong link, change the destination and measure scans.
faq.cancelQuestion: Do QRdx codes stop working if I cancel?

faq.sizeQuestion: How big should a QR code be?
faq.sizeAnswer: About a tenth of the distance it is scanned from, a little more for denser codes: roughly 2.5 to 3 cm for a card held in the hand, 23 cm for a poster 2 m away and about 70 cm for a sign 6 m away. Keep each module at least 0.4 mm and leave a blank margin of four modules around the code.
faq.failQuestion: What makes a printed QR code fail to scan?
faq.failAnswer: The usual causes are low contrast (pale or inverted colours), a missing quiet zone, printing too small for the distance, glare from glossy finishes, and placement on curves, folds or seams. Test the printed proof, not just the file.
faq.formatQuestion: Which file format should I send to the printer?

printSize.metaDescription: Find the minimum printed size for a QR code from the scanning distance, the data it holds and its error-correction level. Results in mm and inches.
printSize.title: QR code print size calculator
printSize.intro1: Printed too small, a QR code fails exactly where it matters: on a poster across the room, a sign by the road or a label on a crowded shelf. Enter how far away people will scan from and what the code contains, and the calculator works out the smallest size that will still scan reliably.
printSize.intro2: It goes beyond the simple distance ÷ 10 rule by accounting for how dense your code is: a long link or a vCard needs more modules than a short URL, so each module, and the whole code, must be printed bigger.
printSize.how1: The content decides the QR version. The calculator picks the smallest version (1 to 40) that holds your text at the chosen error-correction level, using the same capacity tables as the QRdx encoder. Version n is 17 + 4n modules wide.
printSize.how2: The distance decides the module size. The {ratio, number}:1 rule of thumb is treated as describing a simple {reference, number, ::group-off} × {reference, number} code, so each module must be at least distance ÷ ({divisor, number}), and never less than {minimum, number} mm.
printSize.how3: Module size × modules per side gives the code size. Adding {quiet, number} blank modules on each side gives the space the code needs on the page.
printSize.tip1: Keep the content short. A shorter link means a lower version, so the same printed size gives bigger modules.
printSize.tip2: Use dark modules on a light background with strong contrast; inverted or pastel codes fail on some scanners.
printSize.tip3: Test the printed code with several phones at the real distance and lighting before a large print run.
printSize.tip4: Need a code first? Use the <generators>QR code generators</generators> or the <editor>full editor</editor>, then export as SVG for print.

faq.minimumQuestion: What is the minimum size for a QR code?
faq.minimumAnswer: It depends on how far away people scan from and how dense the code is. For a short link scanned from about 25 cm, around 2.5 cm (1 inch) is enough. Whatever the distance, keep each module at least {minimum, number} mm wide so printers and cameras can resolve it.
faq.ruleQuestion: What is the 10:1 rule for QR codes?
faq.ruleAnswer: A common rule of thumb is that a QR code can be scanned from about ten times its width, so a 10 cm code works from about 1 m. It assumes a fairly simple code; codes with more data need to be printed larger, which is what this calculator adjusts for.
faq.logoQuestion: Does a logo or higher error correction change the size?
faq.logoAnswer: Higher error correction adds redundancy, so the same content needs a higher version with more modules, and therefore a larger print. A logo doesn't change the module count, but it hides modules, so use level Q or H when adding one.
faq.quietQuestion: Does the quiet zone count towards the size?
faq.quietAnswer: The code size shown is edge to edge. Scanners also need a blank margin of {quiet, number} modules on every side, which the second figure includes. QRdx downloads have no margin unless you turn on the quiet zone, so leave that space around the code in your layout.
faq.resolutionQuestion: What resolution should I export for print?
faq.resolutionAnswer: Use SVG when you can: it is vector and stays sharp at any size. For PNG, export at least the pixel width shown for 300 DPI, which is the usual minimum for print.

scanChecker.title: QR code scan checker
scanChecker.intro1: Will it scan? Upload, drop or paste a screenshot or photo of any QR code to see what it contains and how reliably it reads, before it goes on a menu, poster or package.
scanChecker.intro2: The checker decodes the code, then shrinks and blurs it the way a phone camera would and tests it again at several sizes, with checks for contrast, clear space and resolution. Everything happens in your browser.
scanChecker.test1: Decoding at 96, 160 and 320 pixels wide with simulated camera blur: roughly a small or distant print, normal phone distance and a close-up.
scanChecker.test2: Contrast between the dark and light modules, measured from the image pixels.
scanChecker.test3: Polarity: light codes on dark backgrounds are not read by every scanner app.
scanChecker.test4: Clear space (the quiet zone) around the code, when the image shows it.
scanChecker.test5: Image resolution: how many pixels each module gets.

faq.uploadAnswer: No. The checker runs entirely in your browser with JavaScript. The image is read on your device and never sent to a server.
faq.scoreQuestion: How is the scan score calculated?
faq.scoreAnswer: The checker finds the code with the open-source jsQR decoder, shrinks it to 96, 160 and 320 pixels wide, adds camera-like blur and contrast loss, and tries to decode it a few times at each size. It then measures the contrast between dark and light modules, whether the code is dark on light, the clear space around it and the image resolution. Each problem lowers the score from 100.
faq.lowQuestion: My code scores low but scans on my phone. Why?
faq.lowAnswer: Phone camera apps are often more forgiving than jsQR, and a photo can lose contrast or sharpness that the printed code doesn't. Treat a low score as a warning that weaker scanners, smaller prints or poor lighting may fail, and test-scan with a few phones before a big print run.
faq.sizeQuestion: How big should a printed QR code be?
faq.sizeAnswer: A common rule of thumb is width ≈ scanning distance ÷ 10, so a code scanned from 20 cm should be about 2 cm wide. Codes holding more data need to be bigger; the print size calculator works it out for you.
faq.fixQuestion: How do I fix a low score?
faq.fixAnswer: Use a dark code on a light background with strong contrast, keep clear space around the code, pick simple square or rounded eyes, choose a higher error-correction level if there is a logo, shorten the content, or print it bigger.

faq.howQuestion: How do I scan a QR code online?
faq.howAnswer: Open this page, tap Start camera and allow camera access, then point your camera at the code. On a laptop or when the code is already on your screen, switch to Image and upload, drag in or paste a screenshot. The result appears under the scanner. Links never open until you tap Open.
faq.safeQuestion: Is it safe to open a link from a QR code?
faq.safeAnswer: Usually, but fake QR codes stuck over real ones ("quishing") are a common scam. Before you open a link, the scanner follows its redirects (up to five) to show where it really ends up{webRisk, select, yes {, checks each address with Google Web Risk} other {}} and looks for common tricks: lookalike letters from other alphabets, bare IP addresses, link shorteners, a fake site name hidden before an @, brand names on unrelated domains, unencrypted pages and app downloads. No check catches everything, so still be careful with sign-in and payment pages.
faq.verifiedAnswer: The link is a real, active dynamic QR code created with QRdx (a qrdx.dev/q/ link{domains, select, yes { or a verified custom domain} other {}}) and has no open abuse reports. It tells you the code is genuine and hasn't been switched off; the code's owner still decides where it points, so the other safety checks still apply.
faq.privateQuestion: Are my scans uploaded or saved?
faq.privateAnswer: No. Camera frames and images are decoded in your browser and never leave your device. Your scan history is stored only in this browser (IndexedDB); you can turn it off, delete single scans or clear it all. To preview a link, only that address is sent to QRdx{webRisk, select, yes { and Google Web Risk} other {}}, and QRdx doesn't keep it. What you scan is kept out of site analytics.
faq.wifiQuestion: Why can't the scanner join a Wi-Fi network for me?
faq.wifiAnswer: Web browsers aren't allowed to change your device's Wi-Fi settings. The scanner shows the network name and lets you copy the password, so you can paste it in your Wi-Fi settings. Your phone's built-in camera app can usually join a Wi-Fi QR code directly.
faq.batchQuestion: Can I scan many codes in a row?
faq.batchAnswer: Yes. Turn on Batch mode and keep pointing the camera at codes, or add several images at once. Each new code is added to the list once, and you can export the batch, or your whole history, as a CSV file.
faq.offlineAnswer: Once you've scanned with it, your browser keeps the scanner page and its decoder, so it opens and reads codes without a connection. Link safety checks need a connection, and links found offline can be checked later from your history.
faq.browsersAnswer: Any modern browser with camera access: Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox on phones and computers. Browsers with a built-in barcode reader (Chrome on Android and macOS) use it directly; others download an open-source decoder (ZXing, compiled to WebAssembly, about 1 MB from the jsDelivr CDN) the first time you scan. The camera needs an https page and your permission.
faq.installQuestion: Can I install the scanner as an app?
faq.installAnswer: Yes. In Chrome, Edge or Samsung Internet, tap Install app under the scanner, or use the browser's own Install option. On iPhone and iPad, tap Add to Home Screen under the scanner for the steps. The app opens straight to the scanner in its own window, works offline once you've scanned with it, and keeps its history on your device.
faq.shareQuestion: Can I scan a QR code from a screenshot?
faq.shareAnswer: Yes. Switch to Image and choose, drop or paste the screenshot. On Android, once the scanner is installed, you can also share a screenshot or photo to QRdx Scanner from any app: it opens and reads the code on your device. Shared images aren't uploaded or kept.

security.metaTitle: Security at QRdx: Sign-in, Data Storage and Reporting Issues
security.metaDescription: How QRdx protects accounts and data: HTTPS with HSTS, a content security policy, passkeys and two-step verification, single sign-on, an audit log, link checks, where data is stored and how to report a vulnerability.
security.title: Security at QRdx
security.intro1: What QRdx does to protect your account, your codes and your visitors' data. Each item describes something that runs on qrdx.dev today, and the code is open source, so you can check it.
security.intro2: QRdx doesn't have SOC 2 or HIPAA certification, or any other security certification, and isn't promising one.

https.title: HTTPS everywhere
https.body: Every page and API call is served over HTTPS, and browsers are told to keep using HTTPS for qrdx.dev for two years (HSTS).

csp.title: Content security policy
csp.body: QRdx's own pages limit which scripts, frames and connections they may load. Pages that show your account's data get a fresh nonce on every request, so a script injected into them doesn't run.

framing.title: No framing by other sites
framing.body: QRdx's own pages can't be shown inside another site's frame, and the screen where you approve an app can't be framed at all. Browsers are also told not to guess file types.

passwords.title: No passwords
passwords.body: You sign in with Google, GitHub or a one-time email code{passkeys, select, yes {, or with a passkey} other {}}. QRdx stores no passwords to leak.

twoFactor.title: Two-step verification
twoFactor.body: A second step with an authenticator app{passkeys, select, yes { or a passkey} other {}}, with backup codes for when you can't use it. Workspaces on Business can require it of every member.

confirm.title: Confirm it's you
confirm.body: Security changes, new API keys and webhooks, role changes and deleting a workspace ask you to confirm it's you, even when you're signed in. A confirmation lasts 10 minutes.

alerts.title: New sign-in alerts
alerts.body: We email you when a browser or device signs in to your account for the first time, and when your two-step verification settings change.

sessions.title: Sign-ins that end
sessions.body: A sign-in lasts 30 days at most, and less if you stop using it. One used from a new country and a new browser must confirm it's you, and you can sign out every other device at once.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.body: OIDC or SAML 2.0 on Business, for an email domain you prove with a DNS record. SAML responses must be signed with SHA-256 or stronger. When a workspace requires it, every other way in is closed for that domain and sessions last 24 hours at most.

roles.title: Roles
roles.body: Owner, admin, member, billing and viewer. Only owners and admins manage people, domains and settings, and billing members and viewers can't change codes.

auditLog.title: Audit log
auditLog.body: On Business, owners and admins see who changed which code, page, member, domain, API key or setting, and can export it as CSV. Rows are kept for {days, number} days.

staff.title: Staff access
staff.body: Only QRdx staff accounts can open the admin tools, and every staff action there is recorded in an audit log.

hashed.title: Hashed keys and tokens
hashed.body: API keys and OAuth access tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, so a copy of the database doesn't reveal them. Passwords on protected codes are stored as hashes too.

encrypted.title: Encrypted integration tokens
encrypted.body: Tokens for the tools you connect, such as Google Drive or Slack, are encrypted with AES-256-GCM.

webhooks.title: Signed webhooks
webhooks.body: Each webhook endpoint has its own secret, and every payload is signed with it, so your server can check it came from QRdx.

linkChecks.title: Link checks
linkChecks.body: When a dynamic code's destination is set, QRdx checks it against Google Web Risk's lists of malware and phishing sites and refuses flagged ones. A destination that couldn't be checked in time is checked again, and its code is switched off if it's flagged.

rateLimits.title: Rate limits
rateLimits.body: The API, the MCP server, forms and other public endpoints are rate limited per key, account or IP address.

bots.title: Bot checks on forms
bots.body: Public forms use Cloudflare Turnstile and hidden fields that only bots fill in.

reports.title: Reporting harmful codes
reports.body: Anyone can <report>report a QR code</report> that leads to phishing, malware or a scam. Codes that break the rules are switched off.

hosting.title: Hosting
hosting.body: The app runs on Vercel. Its server functions run in Washington, D.C., in the United States, behind Vercel's global edge network.

database.title: Database
database.body: Accounts, codes, scans and form responses are kept in a Neon Postgres database in AWS US East (N. Virginia). Neon <neon>encrypts data at rest</neon> with AES-256 and keeps encrypted backups.

files.title: Uploaded files
files.body: Files you upload are stored in Cloudflare R2, in its Asia-Pacific region.

scans.title: Scan data
scans.body: Scanner IP addresses are never stored. Unique visitors are counted with a hash that changes every day.

export.title: Export
export.body: Download everything QRdx keeps about your account as a ZIP from Settings, and export scans, form responses and the audit log as CSV.

delete.title: Deletion
delete.body: Delete codes, pages, files and form responses at any time, or your whole account. Deleted data can stay in the database provider's recovery history for a short time.

dpa.title: Data Processing Addendum
dpa.body: The <dpa>DPA</dpa> is part of the Terms for every customer and includes the Standard Contractual Clauses. Ask for a signed copy if you need one.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.body: The <list>subprocessors list</list> names every service that handles personal data for QRdx, what it does and where. We update it at least 30 days before a new one starts.

params.data: The text or URL to encode, up to {max, number} characters.
params.size: Width and height in pixels, {min, number} to {max, number}. For EPS it's the width in points.

limits.rateTitle: {perMinute, number} requests a minute per IP
limits.rateBody: Over the limit you get a 429 with a Retry-After header. Identical URLs are served from the cache, so showing the same image again rarely reaches the limit.
limits.cacheBody: Same query, same bytes. Responses are sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, so browsers and CDNs keep them. A community item render is cached for 5 minutes, since the item can change.
limits.corsBody: Responses allow every origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *), so browser code can fetch the image as well as show it.
limits.privateTitle: Keep secrets out of the URL
limits.privateBody: The data is part of the URL, so it can end up in server logs, browser history and caches. A Wi-Fi password in a public README is public.
limits.scanTitle: It draws what you ask for
limits.scanBody: The image API doesn't check whether a design scans. Keep strong contrast and test with a phone; the MCP server's design_qr tool checks and repairs a style for you.
limits.selfHostBody: The API is part of the open-source QRdx app, so your own instance serves it at /api/v1/qr on your domain.

faq.freeQuestion: Is there a free QR code API without an API key?
faq.freeAnswer: Yes. GET https://api.qrdx.dev/v1/qr?data=… returns a QR code image with no key, account or signup. It allows {perMinute, number} requests a minute per IP address, and identical URLs are cached for a year.
faq.logoQuestion: Can the QR code API add a logo?
faq.logoAnswer: Yes. logoIcon puts a quick icon (Wi-Fi, link, phone, email and more) or any of {brands} brand logos from Simple Icons in the center, with no key. The code switches to error correction H when the logo needs it, so it still scans.
faq.formatsQuestion: Which image formats does it return?
faq.formatsAnswer: SVG by default, or PNG, lossless WebP and vector EPS with format=png, webp or eps. Sizes go from {min, number} to {max, number} pixels.
faq.expireAnswer: No. The image API makes static codes: what you encode is inside the code, so it works for as long as the link or text in it does. Nothing expires and nothing counts scans.
faq.dynamicQuestion: Can I change where a code points after printing?
faq.dynamicAnswer: Not with the image API. For that you need a dynamic code, created in the QRdx dashboard or with the REST API and a free API key. The free plan includes {count, number} dynamic codes with unlimited scans.
faq.googleQuestion: Can it replace the Google Chart QR code API?
faq.googleAnswer: Yes. Change the host and path, rename chl to data and chs to size (QR codes are square, so one number), and set level and margin from chld. Parameters it doesn't know, such as cht and choe, are ignored. The migration guide has the full mapping.
faq.limitQuestion: What happens if I go over the rate limit?
faq.limitAnswer: You get a 429 response with a Retry-After header saying when to try again. Identical URLs are cached for a year, so an image shown on a busy page is usually served from the cache.
faq.aiQuestion: Can an AI assistant use it?
faq.aiAnswer: Yes. The QRdx MCP server's generate_qr_code tool returns these image URLs, and an assistant without MCP can write the URL itself as a Markdown image.

faq.freeQuestion: Can I make a dynamic QR code for free?
faq.freeAnswer: Yes. A free QRdx account includes {count, number} active dynamic codes with unlimited scans and {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} of scan history, with no trial period. Archived codes don't count toward the limit, and paid plans remove it.
faq.expireAnswer: Not on QRdx. A code keeps redirecting until you pause, archive or delete it, or until an end date or scan limit you set yourself. That holds on every plan, Free included, and after a downgrade, a failed payment or a cancellation. The one exception is abuse: a code that points to phishing or malware is disabled.
faq.editQuestion: Can I edit a QR code after it's printed?
faq.editAnswer: Only a dynamic one. It holds a short link, so you change the destination in the dashboard and the printed code opens the new page on the next scan. A static code holds the address itself, so changing it means printing a new code.
faq.trackQuestion: How do I track QR code scans?
faq.trackAnswer: Make the code dynamic. Each dynamic code has an analytics page with scans over time, unique visitors, countries and cities, devices, operating systems, browsers, referrers and languages, and you can export the scans as CSV. QRdx doesn't store IP addresses or count known bots and link previews.
faq.typesQuestion: Can a Wi-Fi or vCard QR code be dynamic?
faq.typesAnswer: Not directly, because the phone reads Wi-Fi and vCard details from the pattern itself, and a dynamic code can only open a link. For contact details you want to change later, point a dynamic code at a hosted contact page. For Wi-Fi, use a static code.
faq.domainQuestion: Can I use my own domain for the short links?
faq.domainAnswer: Yes, on {plans}. The code then holds a link like go.yourbrand.com/menu, and redirects and scan analytics work the same way. You connect the domain by adding a DNS record at your DNS provider.
faq.apiQuestion: Can I create dynamic QR codes with an API?
faq.apiAnswer: Yes. The REST API creates and edits codes and reads their scans, with an API key or an OAuth access token. Free accounts get {perDay, number} requests a day, and paid plans can create up to {batch} codes in one request.
faq.selfHostQuestion: Can I run dynamic QR codes on my own server?
faq.selfHostAnswer: Yes. QRdx is open source, and a self-hosted copy runs dynamic codes, hosted pages and scan analytics on your own domain. Scan locations depend on what your host's headers provide, which the self-hosting guide explains.

faq.githubQuestion: Where is the QRdx source code on GitHub?

faq.freeAnswer: Yes. There's no license fee; you pay only for your own server and database. A self-hosted instance runs dynamic codes, hosted pages and scan analytics. Single sign-on and the audit log stay off unless you have a QRdx license key.
faq.needQuestion: What do I need to self-host QRdx?

faq.closedQuestion: Can I use the QR code library in a closed-source app?

faq.changesQuestion: Do I have to publish my changes to the app?
faq.changesAnswer: Only when you run a modified version as a network service: then you have to offer its source code to its users under the same license. If you plan to build on the app, check that the AGPL fits your project first.
faq.nameQuestion: Can I call my fork QRdx?
faq.nameAnswer: No. A fork or a public service built from the code needs its own name and logo, and the license notices stay. Running QRdx for yourself or your organization under its own name is fine. The trademark policy has the details.
faq.shutdownQuestion: What happens to my qrdx.dev codes if QRdx shuts down?
